mcq.question: Which open mode keeps the existing contents of a log file and adds new lines at the end?
mcq.explanation: With `app`, every write is appended regardless of the current position. `trunc` empties the file on open, and `ate` only positions the stream at the end once, at open time.

mcq.question: Why are telemetry samples written field by field instead of with `out.write(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(&sample), sizeof sample)`?

options.B: Dumping the struct copies padding bytes and the machine's own byte order, so the file is not portable
options.C: Writing field by field makes the file smaller only on Windows

mcq.explanation: A struct's memory layout includes compiler-chosen padding and native endianness. Writing each field in a fixed byte order produces the same file on every platform.

bonus.question: Text logs are easy to read; binary files are compact and fast. For a flight recorder, which data belongs in which format, and why?
Write a failing test for a `rotate_log(path, max_bytes)` function that renames the log to `.1` once it grows past a limit, then implement it with std::filesystem.
